These are selected starting points. The full annotated collection, source perspectives, inspection limits and remaining research questions follow below. A starting guide is not an exhaustive history or community endorsement.

01

Identity and context

The Catawba Nation is a contemporary tribal nation with deep connections to the Carolinas.

Read the sources [1] newrivercatawba.org

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Catawba-authored history, language, pottery, land and governance. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] newrivercatawba.org [2] saponi-catawbanation.org [3] Catawba Nation

03

River communities, trade and adaptation

The Nation’s history describes villages, farming and fishing along the Catawba River, followed by expanding trade and colonial pressure. It also explains how outsiders extended the name Catawba across river-valley communities. This is the Nation’s own historical account; its estimates and interpretations should be distinguished from the original records still to inspect.

Read the sources [3] Catawba Nation

04

A name across changing political relationships

David G. Moore’s scholarly account treats the historical Catawba Nation as a coalition shaped by colonial trade, conflict and refuge. It helps explain why one old label may involve several community histories. That historical process does not automatically establish the current affiliation of another community or organization.

Read the sources [4] David G. Moore / NCpedia, Library of North Carolina; University of North Carolina Press article

05

The river in contemporary institutional work

The Environmental Protections Division connects its work with the Nation’s river setting. Its public account describes air and water programmes, monitoring, natural-resource management and community infrastructure responsibilities. These are stated areas of work and development, not independently measured environmental outcomes or a map of present legal boundaries.

Read the sources [5] Catawba Nation

About the Nation — Catawba history and river relationships ↗

The Nation’s own historical account connects river villages, farming, trade and adaptation. Its perspective is distinct from the other organizational reading leads inherited by this broader entry.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete We are Proud of our Past historical unit through the Merrell reference. Later heritage narratives, pottery-maker biographies and current membership figures were not adopted.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal public HTTP 200 body read. No underlying colonial journals, treaty, land deeds, historic census or pottery objects inspected. Chronological estimates, warfare superlatives, current legal claims and population/acreage figures are not independently verified or adopted.

https://www.catawba.com/about-the-nation
History·River communities
Scholarly reference / university-press articleDavid G. Moore / NCpedia, Library of North Carolina; University of North Carolina Press articleSource 4

Catawba People — selected historical context ↗

A named scholarly reference distinguishes the historical Catawba coalition from a single unchanged community. Read its account of colonial trade and refugees alongside the Nation’s own history.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Opening historical paragraphs from The Catawba people are often referred to as the Catawba Nation through the 1750s/French-and-Indian-War discussion, before Reeling from the effects. Author/date and 2025 revision credit read; later current totals and casino/legal material not used.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal public HTTP 200 text read. Copyright notice restricts redistribution; no source text, historical map or pottery image is reproduced publicly. Original ethnographies, colonial records and linked publications uninspected. Period labels and refugee movement do not establish present affiliation, and wording implying disappearance of other peoples is not adopted.

https://www.ncpedia.org/catawba-indians

Environmental Protections Division ↗

The Nation describes water, air and environmental-monitoring responsibilities within its river setting. These are the department’s public aims and work categories, not independently assessed results.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Complete Environmental Protections Division body from its geographic introduction through the department list, before Division Contacts. Staff contacts and linked drinking-water reports excluded.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Normal public HTTP 200 prose read. No monitoring dataset, water-quality report, maps, boundary records or current environmental-condition assessment inspected. Programme development and stewardship are stated responsibilities; no claim every goal has been achieved.

https://www.catawba.com/environmental-services
